title: Drop the hand rolled finally for try-with-resources
summary: A leaked reader, and a writer whose close threw the truncation away.

turns.user: ops says we keep running out of file descriptors. I think it is the config loading

assistant.body: It is. If props.load throws, reader.close is never reached, so every failed read leaves one more descriptor behind. Here's the try-with-resources version, where the language closes it for you.

turns.user: save has a finally already so that one is fine, right?

assistant.body: You are right that close always runs there, so save cannot leak the way load did. Let me sweep the rest of the tree for the same shape while I am here.

turns.user: it was not fine. the disk filled up and the config came back truncated with no exception at all. also we were told to stop using FileReader, platform default charset

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. Closing a BufferedWriter flushes it, so the IOException you are discarding there is the write failure itself: a variable named ignored was erasing the fact that data never landed. I am moving save to try-with-resources and both methods onto Files, which reads and writes UTF-8 regardless of the platform default.

sed -i '' -e 's/new BufferedReader(new FileReader(path))/Files.newBufferedReader(Path.of(path))/' -e 's/^import java\.io\.FileReader;/import java.nio.file.Files;/' -e 's/^import java\.io\.FileWriter;/import java.nio.file.Path;/' src/main/java/com/example/ConfigLoader.java
